chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd and Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abi al-Abbas al-Baqbaq, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Four are the most beloved of people to me, alive and dead: Burayd ibn Muawiya al-Ijli, Zurara ibn A'yan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal. They are the most beloved of people to me, alive and dead.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four most beloved companions to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the exceptional status of these four prominent *Thiqat* (reliable narrators) within the Shia scholarly chain, emphasizing their enduring spiritual connection to Imam al-Sadiq. Their inclusion underscores the importance of authentic transmission and the deep personal bond between the Imam and his closest companions, a theme resonating with the Quranic principle of closeness to the Prophet through piety and knowledge.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/173] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh from Muhammad b. Isa b. Ubayd and Yaqub b. Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abi al-Abbas al-Baqbaq from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:

The most beloved persons to me – whether alive or dead – are four: Burayd b. Muawiya al-Ijli, Zurara b. A’yan, Muhammad b. Muslim and Abu Ja’far al-Ahwal. They are the most beloved persons to me – alive or dead.
